slides.title: Binary Search Operations
slides.prompt: C++ provides efficient binary search algorithms for sorted ranges: std::binary_search, std::lower_bound, std::upper_bound, and std::equal_range, operating in O(log N) time.

slides.title: Boolean Binary Search
slides.prompt: Fill in the function returning true if a target value exists in a sorted range.

slides.title: lower_bound Definition
slides.prompt: What does std::lower_bound(begin, end, val) return?
options: Iterator to the first element that is NOT less than val (>= val)
Iterator to the first element strictly less than val
Iterator to the last element equal to val
slides.correctAnswer: Iterator to the first element that is NOT less than val (>= val)

slides.title: Upper Bound Search
slides.prompt: Fill in the algorithm returning an iterator to the first element strictly greater than val.

slides.title: std::equal_range Return Type
slides.prompt: What type of result does std::equal_range return?
options: A pair of iterators representing [lower_bound, upper_bound)
A vector containing all matching elements
The total count integer of matching values
slides.correctAnswer: A pair of iterators representing [lower_bound, upper_bound)

slides.title: Equal Range Function
slides.prompt: Fill in the algorithm function used to find lower and upper bounds simultaneously.

slides.title: Binary Search Requirement
slides.prompt: What is the critical prerequisite for calling std::binary_search or std::lower_bound?
options: The input range must be sorted according to the ordering criterion
The container must be a std::vector
The container size must be a power of 2
Elements must be unique with no duplicates
slides.correctAnswer: The input range must be sorted according to the ordering criterion

slides.title: Merging Sorted Ranges
slides.prompt: Fill in the algorithm function that merges two sorted ranges into a single sorted range.

slides.title: std::includes Purpose
slides.prompt: What does std::includes(beg1, end1, beg2, end2) evaluate?
options: Returns true if every element in the second sorted range is present in the first sorted range
Returns true if two ranges share at least one common value
Returns true if the ranges are identical in length and content
Merges two ranges if they overlap
slides.correctAnswer: Returns true if every element in the second sorted range is present in the first sorted range

slides.title: Set Difference Operation
slides.prompt: Fill in the algorithm function that computes the set difference of two sorted ranges.
